facts.statement: Ornithosuchus was first described by Newton in 1894.
Fossils of Ornithosuchus date to the Late Triassic period.
Ornithosuchus has traditionally been estimated to be about 4 meters long.
facts.quote: Ornithosuchus has traditionally been estimated at a length around 4 m.

facts.statement: Only one species, O. woodwardi, is currently recognized for Ornithosuchus, while O. taylori is considered a synonym.
facts.quote: A single species of Ornithosuchus is recognized, O. woodwardi; O. taylori is a synonym.

facts.statement: Recent studies have revised the maximum length of Ornithosuchus to 2.2 meters.
facts.quote: The maximal length of Ornithosuchus was revised to 2.2 m.

facts.statement: Ornithosuchus is the type genus of the family Ornithosuchidae, which included geographically widespread, facultatively bipedal carnivores in the Late Triassic.
facts.quote: Ornithosuchus is the type genus of the Ornithosuchidae, a family of facultatively biped carnivores that were geographically widespread during the Late Triassic.

facts.statement: Ornithosuchus belongs to the unranked order Crurotarsi.
Ornithosuchus is classified within the family Ornithosuchidae.
The type species of Ornithosuchus is O. longidens, originally named Dasygnathus longidens.

facts.statement: Ornithosuchus lived between 237 and 205.7 million years ago, spanning the Carnian to Norian stages.
